# Lab 3 (part 1) – Cutting Application: Step-by-Step Guide

S7-1214C · TIA Portal V16 · language: **FBD** · four pneumatic cylinders C1–C4 on a plywood plate

---

## 0. Goal in One Paragraph

A cut-off device with four cylinders must run a fixed sequence after the **Start** button: wait 2 s, lock the feeder (C1), feed material (C2), lock the cutter (C3), cut (C4), then retract everything and **stop** until Start is pressed again. **Stop** aborts the sequence at any time.

---

## 1. Sequence (from the time diagram, Figure 2)

| Step | What happens | Transition to next step |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Idle | Start pressed (I1.1) |
| 1 | Withdrawal period | 2 s elapsed |
| 2 | **C1 out** (feeder lock) | C1 out position (I0.1) |
| 3 | **C2 out** (feeder pushes material) | C2 out position (I0.3) |
| 4 | **C3 out** (cutting lock) | C3 out position (I0.5) |
| 5 | **C4 out** (cut) **and C1 in** (feeder lock released) | C4 out (I0.7) **and** C1 in (I0.0) |
| 6 | **C4 in** and **C2 in** | C4 in (I0.6) **and** C2 in (I0.2) |
| 7 | **C3 in** | C3 in position (I0.4) → back to step 0 |

Check against Figure 2: C1 retracts while C4 cuts, C2 retracts together with C4, C3 retracts last. If your instructor expects a purely sequential retract (one cylinder per step), insert extra steps – the structure is the same.

Outputs per step (single-acting cylinders, coil on = out, off = spring return):

| Output | On in steps |
|---|---|
| Q0.0 (C1 out) | 2, 3, 4 |
| Q0.1 (C2 out) | 3, 4, 5 |
| Q0.2 (C3 out) | 4, 5, 6 |
| Q0.3 (C4 out) | 5 |

---

## 2. I/O Table (Annex 1)

| Address | Meaning | Suggested symbol |
|---|---|---|
| I1.1 | Start pushbutton | `Start` |
| I1.2 | Stop pushbutton | `Stop` |
| I0.0 / I0.1 | C1 in / out position | `C1_in` / `C1_out` |
| I0.2 / I0.3 | C2 in / out position | `C2_in` / `C2_out` |
| I0.4 / I0.5 | C3 in / out position | `C3_in` / `C3_out` |
| I0.6 / I0.7 | C4 in / out position | `C4_in` / `C4_out` |
| Q0.0 … Q0.3 | Valves C1 … C4 out | `C1_Valve` … `C4_Valve` |

Station facts: output terminals 1–6 (1+2 supply, 3–6 = Q0.0–Q0.3), input terminals 16–23 = I0.0–I1.0, lowest row = 24 V sources. Check on the station that the Start/Stop buttons really are on I1.1/I1.2.

Internal tags (create in the tag table):

| Tag | Address | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `Start_Edge_Mem` | M0.0 | P_TRIG memory |
| `StartPulse` | M1.0 | Start rising edge |
| `St1`…`St7` | M10.1…M10.7 | Step bits |
| `Running` | M11.0 | Any step active |
| `T2s_Q` | M11.1 | 2 s timer done |

---

## 3. Safety

- Electrical **and compressed air** equipment – **risk of crushing**. Keep hands out of the cylinder area when air is on.
- Depressurize the equipment before checking connections. Ask the staff how to switch the pressure on **before the first test**.
- The hardware is pre-connected, but verify the connections at the start.

## 4. Step-by-Step

### Step 1 – Understand the equipment
Read the introduction, identify cylinders C1–C4, their magnetic limit sensors (in/out) and the SMC valves (24 V DC). Ask the instructor if unclear.

### Step 2 – Project and hardware test
1. New TIA project, add the correct CPU (S7-1214C, exact order number).
2. Download the HW config and an empty program. Fix any problems with the instructor.

### Step 3 – Tag table
Enter all I/O tags and internal tags from Section 2.

### Step 4 – Program (FBD), FC1 called from OB1
Create FC1 `CuttingSequence` (FBD) and build the 11 networks as in `Lab3_1_FBD_Sketch.png`:

| Net | Content |
|---|---|
| 1 | `P_TRIG` (M_BIT = M0.0): CLK = Start (I1.1) → `StartPulse` M1.0 |
| 2 | `>=1` of St1…St7 → `Running` M11.0 |
| 3 | `TON` IN = St1, PT = `T#2s` → Q → `T2s_Q` M11.1 |
| 4 | **St1** `SR`: S = `StartPulse` AND NOT `Running`; R1 = St2 OR Stop |
| 5 | **St2** `SR`: S = St1 AND `T2s_Q`; R1 = St3 OR Stop |
| 6 | **St3** `SR`: S = St2 AND I0.1; R1 = St4 OR Stop |
| 7 | **St4** `SR`: S = St3 AND I0.3; R1 = St5 OR Stop |
| 8 | **St5** `SR`: S = St4 AND I0.5; R1 = St6 OR Stop |
| 9 | **St6** `SR`: S = St5 AND I0.7 AND I0.0; R1 = St7 OR Stop |
| 10 | **St7** `SR`: S = St6 AND I0.6 AND I0.2; R1 = (St7 AND I0.4) OR Stop |
| 11 | Outputs: Q0.0 = St2∨St3∨St4; Q0.1 = St3∨St4∨St5; Q0.2 = St4∨St5∨St6; Q0.3 = St5 |

How it works: each step bit is set when the previous step is active **and** its transition condition (sensor) is true, and is reset when the **next** step becomes active (or on Stop). The last step resets itself when C3 is in, so the machine returns to idle. Using `SR` (reset-dominant) guarantees that **Stop always wins**. One scan of overlap between two steps is harmless.

Tips:
- `>=1` with 7 inputs: right-click an input → *Insert input*.
- Right-click an input pin → *Invert RLO* for NOT.
- Add comments per network, call FC1 in OB1.

### Step 5 – Download and test (pressure on only after the first dry run)
1. Compile, download OB1 + FC1.
2. **Dry run without air:** monitor OB1/FC1, press Start, push the cylinders / sensors by hand (or force inputs in a watch table) and watch the steps advance.
3. With the instructor: switch on the pressure and test the real sequence.

### Step 6 – Test table

| # | Test | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Start | after 2 s: C1 out |
| 2 | C1 reaches out position | C2 out |
| 3 | C2 reaches out | C3 out |
| 4 | C3 reaches out | C4 out (cut) and C1 retracts |
| 5 | C4 out and C1 in | C4 and C2 retract |
| 6 | C4 in and C2 in | C3 retracts |
| 7 | C3 in | all off, machine idle; nothing moves |
| 8 | Press Start again | cycle repeats |
| 9 | Press Stop during the cycle | all outputs off, cylinders spring back, idle |
| 10 | Press Start while running | ignored |

### Step 7 – Present
Demonstrate the function, show hardware configuration, program and tag table.

---

## 5. Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause |
|---|---|
| Sequence stalls at a step | Sensor not detecting (check magnet position, LED on sensor) or wrong input address |
| Cylinder moves the wrong cylinder | Output/valve assignment differs from Annex 1 – check terminals |
| Nothing starts | Stop wired NC (invert) or `Running` stuck (a step bit still 1 → press Stop once) |
| Start restarts immediately after cycle | Start button held down – cycle needs a **new** rising edge |
